key_insight: Adaptive syndrome skipping in surface-GKP codes can cut outer-code measurement overhead by deciding, round by round, whether to measure Z, X, both, or neither based on analog reliability information from inner GKP correction.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to lower gate, ancilla, and noise overhead in fault-tolerant quantum processors while preserving logical error performance.
method: Use analog information from inner GKP correction to estimate syndrome reliability.
Compare the benefit of reusing the previous syndrome versus performing a fresh noisy extraction.
Select among four actions each round: measure Z, measure X, measure both, or skip both and reuse prior syndromes.
evidence_signal: Circuit-level simulations in the abstract report fewer surface-code stabilizer measurements with logical error rates comparable to or better than the full-measurement baseline, especially when gate and measurement noise exceed idle noise.
watch_item: The scheme’s gains depend on the relative noise model and reliable access to analog GKP information, so performance may be sensitive to hardware-specific calibration and implementation details.
paper_title: When to Skip Syndrome Extraction in Surface-GKP Codes
